newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end up as golds rally.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end up as golds rally.

text.p: South African shares had a healthy Thursday and ended firmly in positive territory after being helped by a firmer gold sector and a bullish short-term outlook for major international markets, dealers said.
The bullion price -- which on Wednesday hit its lowest level since October 4, 1993 -- rallied slightly and dragged South Africa's bombed out gold shares up with it.
Industrial shares had a firmer day on the back of healthy demand for a wide-range of stocks, especially blue-chips, and a bullish outlook for major international markets.

London shares rose further into record territory by early afternoon as a rise in U.S. treasury bonds pointed to a higher opening on Wall Street after profit-taking on Wednesday ended a recent surge in New York.
The all-share index rose 27.6 points to finish at 6,779 as the industrials index jumped 45.7 points to 8,176.4.

Gold shares had a good day with the index rising just under percent, or 12.6 points, to 1,421 as the first day of the quarterly reporting season kicked off with Goldfields announcing healthy third quarter results.
